facts.fact: 叙述者常与一位老人一起打猎：擦枪、磨刀、做三明治，天不亮就出发。
facts.anchor: We hunt this way together often now.

facts.fact: 老人打趣女儿们「打猎」只会从他的冰箱里取肉。
facts.anchor: I spose you gonna hunt just like my girls—out of my freezer.

facts.fact: 第二节：男孩们进屋时神色古怪、异常安静，默默烧水洗手、倒空口袋里的子弹壳和火柴。
facts.anchor: The boys came in looking kind of funny. Awfully quiet, too. No teasing. Just set themselves to cleaning up.

facts.fact: 男孩们惊动了坟地，遇到了传说中每四十年出现一次的「鹿身人灵」。
facts.anchor: It was that man-deer spirit that’s said to appear when them graves have been disturbed.

facts.fact: 第三节：女人们设局报复——骗丈夫们去「猎」混血女人 Sarah Goes Lightning，两棵树上挂的两头鹿也是她们所为。
facts.anchor: how they tricked their husbands into hunting for that half-blood woman Sarah Goes Lightning.

facts.fact: 老人举着一杆挂着鹿心的棍子，声称与巨兽搏斗才保住这颗心——其实他只是喂了只黄鼠狼。
facts.anchor: “Had to fight a great big animal to save this heart for youse girls.”

facts.fact: 结尾：清晨两人偷偷出门打猎，叙述者压低声音像念老故事的最后一行，等谁应一声「Aho」。
facts.anchor: “Going hunting,” I say, dropping my voice like it’s the last line in some old story—like someone is going to answer, Aho.
